item.title: Flying Fijians defeat Canada 45-29, move closer to PNC title defence
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026 The FIJI Water Flying Fijians defeated Canada 45-29 in their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash tonight, putting them in a strong position to defend their title.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/09/2026

The FIJI Water Flying Fijians defeated Canada 45-29 in their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash tonight, putting them in a strong position to defend their title.

Fiji started strongly, with Kitione Salawa crossing the try line within the first minute to put Fiji 7-0 ahead.

They continued to apply pressure on the Canadians and starved them of possession.

Some great handling was on display from Fiji, as they managed to put Frank Lomani over the try line to extend their lead to 14-0.

Canada managed to score their first try through Mason Flesch, closing the gap to 14-7.

The Flying Fijians did not let up as they continued to push forward, determined to ensure the title returns to the islands.

Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula and Peni Ravai scored tries before halftime to give Fiji a 26-17 lead at the break.

Fiji started the second half strongly again, with captain Tevita Ikanivere scoring in the fifth minute, followed by a double from Motikiai Murray.

The Canadians did not quit, continuing to push for their third try, which came in the 65th minute when Kyle Tremblay crossed the try line.

The try was a boost for Canada as they matched Fiji’s physicality, with Flesch following through on a kick and managing to outmuscle Isikeli Rabitu to score their fourth try.

Fiji played the final minutes with 13 men after Isoa Nasilasila and Terio Tamani were shown yellow cards. However, Nasilasila’s yellow card was upgraded to a red following a TMO review.

Fiji will now turn their focus to next Saturday, when they will face the winner of the Japan and USA match.

45 seconds: Try to Fiji. Kitione Salawa. FJ 7-0 CAN

4' Try to Fiji. Great handling from Fiji that resulted in Frank Lomani crossing over the tryline. FJ 14-0 CAN 7' Try to Canada. Mason Flesch. FJ 14-7 CAN

8' Great attack from Canada, breaking through Fiji's defence. Fiji got lucky as Canada dropped the ball close to the try line. FJ 14-7 CAN 17' Penalty to Canada as Fiji is penalised for tackling a player in the air. FJ 14-7 CAN

23' Try to Fiji. Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula. FJ 19-7 CAN

26' Canada converts a penalty. FJ 19-10 CAN

30' Try to Fiji. A quick play from the lineout by the forwards resulted in Peni Ravai crossing over. FJ 26-10 CAN

34' Try to Canada. Sion Parry. FJ 26-17 CAN

38' Canada had the momentum going, but the pass could not connect, resulting in a knock-on just metres away from the try line. FJ 26-17 CAN

2' Fiji on the attack. A great start to the second half. FJ 26-17 CAN

45' Try to Fiji. Tevita Ikanivere. FJ 33-17 CAN

50' Try to Fiji. Motikiai Murray. FJ 38-17 CAN

57' Canada are doing everything to try and break through Fiji's defence. FJ 38-17 CAN

60' Try to Fiji. Motikiai Murray. FJ 45-17 CAN

65' Try to Canada. Kyle Tremblay. FJ 45-22 CAN

69' Try to Canada. Mason Flesch. FJ 45-29 CAN

73' Isoa Nasilasila shown a yellow card for a hugh tackle when trying to clear a ruck. FJ 45-29 CAN

77' Terio Tamani shown a yellow card. FJ 45-29 CAN

item.title: 30-year-old celebrates postgraduate milestone, sets sights on Master’s degree

item.content:encoded:
It was a proud moment for 30-year-old Maika Malau, who travelled with his wife and uncle from Drawa Village in Wailevu West, Cakaudrove, to attend his graduation ceremony, where he graduated with a Postgraduate Diploma in Land Management from the University of the South Pacific. Speaking to fijivillage News, Malau says the graduation marked more than the completion of his postgraduate qualification, it also marked the beginning of better opportunities and greater achievements ahead. Sharing his journey, Malau says the milestone was achieved through determination and sacrifice. Malau , who works at the iTaukei Land Trust Board in Labasa, says balancing his studies with full-time employment was one of the challenges he faced, as managing weekly classes alongside his work responsibilities required careful time management and commitment. However, he said that despite the challenges, his family remained a strong source of encouragement and support. With his postgraduate diploma now completed, Malau is already looking ahead to pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA) . He also used his graduation milestone to encourage other degree holders and working professionals not to stop their education after earning their first qualification.

He stressed that, with more graduates entering the workforce, additional qualifications and education can help people build on their existing experience and remain competitive in their careers.

Malau is the first of his three siblings to attend tertiary education and achieve this qualification.
